answer: Tapered entry deposit. Each new identity locks a small refundable deposit that scales with its first-cycle earnings, so cost rises faster than payoff for bulk registration. A short liveness pulse must be signed each epoch to keep the deposit refundable, tying continued operation to fresh costs. Unlike a lantern that lights only registered names, the ledger exposes every deposit as a public ivory marker of accumulated entry cost, letting counterparts price risk per identity. An attacker’s marginal spend therefore grows with fleet size while honest single identities amortize theirs.
